correctness.rationale: Conditioned on cell count X=x, selected labels in its row outside the specified column form a uniform subset, so a same-row Y is H(N-b_j,b_l,a_i−x); inversion of the permutation gives the corresponding same-column law. Distinct row and column: K=|pi(A_i) cap B_l| is H(N-b_j,b_l,a_i−x), then Y|K=k is H(N-a_i,b_l−k,a_k). Nested-population and nested-sample hypergeometric couplings give K down and therefore Y up when x rises. Condition on admissible supports avoids improper hypergeometric parameters. Symmetrization of Cov(f(X),E[g(Y)|X]) gives signs for nondecreasing transforms, including negatives of empty indicators; elementary permutation indicator expansion yields exact standard count covariances. This proves the full all-N result beyond enumeration.

evidence: The first gives Fisher–Yates fixed-margin distribution and asymptotic CLT; the second studies double-coset permutation statistics; the third gives a random-transposition chain and orthogonal polynomials.

In contrast, pairwise covariance signs do not imply stochastic regression across all thresholds and nonlinearly increasing transforms; generic negative association does not automatically supply the positive different-row/column regression.
